artifact_role: SNARK-origin proofcore recovery session review; not canonical release
interpretation: rev0851 correctly found the evidence-vault mission, but rev0852 refines it: the evidence vault should serve a recoverable proofcore.
key_findings: User-provided history says the project began as a SNARKs-adjacent proof exploration. The carried canonical indexes support a still-visible proof lineage across zkrtp, streamfold, sumcheck/FRI/PCS/Halo2 ABI IR, receipts, attestations, witnesses, and verifiers.

The carried canonical index exposes 1067 broad proof-signal paths, but 0 of those paths are present as payload files in this overlay ZIP. The overlay is therefore a map to the proof core, not the proof core itself.
The rights ledger records zkrtp as 193 files / 18,902,244 bytes and streamfold as 83 files / 2,778,263 bytes, both represented without retained source/root and both blocked pending license decisions.

The index suggests a rich proof-adjacent ecosystem, but the overlay does not expose an executable contract that binds claims to verifier code, circuit/constraint representations, public inputs, witness policy, parameters, and expected outputs.

The project hardened publication, symlink, overlay, and rights boundaries repeatedly. That work is useful, but the new origin context implies it may have displaced the older proof question instead of completing it.

No root LICENSE/COPYING/NOTICE, component license conclusions, or missing local rights target has been resolved. The proof-origin context does not reduce the publication rights block; it increases the need for source/root clarity.
next_best_step: Mount or recover the full canonical tree and build a canonical-path-to-role proofcore map, beginning with zkrtp and streamfold.
user_context: Project began as a SNARKs-adjacent proof exploration and this was the core for most of its life.
